_comment: V5 KV3 no-loop falsifier. Reproduces the shipped KV3 rank and the counterfactual rank without the no-loop key over the schema-1.7 out-v5 scans; includes the per-leaf source evidence for the three pre-registered Q3 targets.

targets.leaf_evidence: per-printable-byte leaf: no loop inside; branch ladder decides collect vs. direct write, then stores one cell byte at `screen-write.c:2830`; called from `input.c:1244` and `input.c:2892` (pre-registered Q3).

per-measurement leaf: no loop inside; starts the wall clock, spawns the child and blocks in `wait4` (`src/timer/unix_timer.rs:33-41`), so wall-clock time is dominated by the child wait (pre-registered Q3).

per-item allocation leaf: no loop inside; one allocator call plus `memset` (`cJSON.c:243-246`), called for the root, every array element, every object member, every string and every number temp (pre-registered Q3).

verdict: PARTIALLY FALSIFIED - the no-loop guard demotes all three pre-registered Q3 targets (3/3), but removing only the no-loop term does NOT restore any to the inline top 8 (shipped->counterfactual ranks: tmux 820->325, hyperfine 58->46, cJSON 60->45; top 8). The guard is a contributing demotion, not the sole cause of the Q3 recall miss: the static-cost key cannot surface per-byte/per-call leaves (the V1 H1 prediction for call weights). V7 must adopt call-weighted/per-iteration cost (or a separate call-frequency view), not merely drop the guard; a two-list variant of the same static cost is insufficient. Note cJSON cJSON_New_Item is also reachable_from_entry=false in the default-tier call graph, so a reachable-only Q3 (R-pf-098) would hide it further.
